name: Part
simple: Part is the basic building block of Roblox: the plain block you get when you click Part in Studio. It can be one of five shapes: Block, Ball, Cylinder, Wedge, or CornerWedge. Everything a part can do (Position, Color, Anchored, Touched, and more) comes from BasePart.
analogy: Parts are like LEGO bricks. You can make them any size and color and stack them to build anything, and the Shape setting is like choosing a square brick, a round one, or a ramp piece.
whenToUse: Build floors, walls, platforms, and obstacles.
Spawn simple objects from code, like coins, bullets, or falling blocks.
Make a round ball or a ramp by changing `Shape`.
where: Lives in Workspace to be seen and do physics. Create one in code with `Instance.new("Part")`, or insert it in Studio from the Home or Model tab.

terms.BasePart: The family that Part belongs to. Look there for Position, Size, Color, Anchored, Touched, and other shared features.
terms.Enum: A fixed list of choices. `Enum.PartType` is the list of shapes a Part can be.
terms.stud: Roblox's unit of distance. A brand-new Part is 4 studs long, 1 stud tall, and 2 studs wide.

examples.title: Rain bouncy balls from the sky
examples.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

for i = 1, 10 do
	local ball = Instance.new("Part")
	ball.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
	ball.Size = Vector3.new(3, 3, 3)
	ball.Color = Color3.fromRGB(math.random(0, 255), math.random(0, 255), math.random(0, 255))
	-- random spot 40 studs up, somewhere between -20 and 20 on X and Z
	ball.Position = Vector3.new(math.random(-20, 20), 40, math.random(-20, 20))
	ball.Parent = Workspace -- not anchored, so it falls
	task.wait(0.5)
end
explain: `Instance.new("Part")` makes a part; setting `Shape` to Ball makes it round.
Each ball gets a random color and a random spot 40 studs up.
They are not anchored, so gravity pulls them down. One drops every half second.

gotchas: A Ball always stays perfectly round, so its three Size numbers are kept equal. Use a MeshPart if you want an oval.
New parts are not anchored, so they fall. Set `Anchored = true` for things that should stay put.

Part.Shape.simple: Which shape the part is: Block (box, the default), Ball (sphere), Cylinder (tube lying along the X axis), Wedge (a ramp), or CornerWedge (a corner ramp). For fancier shapes use a MeshPart or solid modeling.
Part.Shape.example:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
part.Size = Vector3.new(6, 2, 2) -- 6 long along X, 2 across
part.Anchored = true
part.Parent = Workspace
